key_insight: DITL improves mammography classification by adapting transfer learning to dataset-specific difficulty and neighborhood structure instead of using fixed generic losses.
engineering_relevance: The framework is practical for medical imaging pipelines because it adds little computational cost while scaling from small lesion datasets to large clinical cohorts.
method: A-DWCE weights each sample by k-nearest-neighbor label purity in a self-supervised feature space.
A-NR-Triplet uses neighborhood-based triplet supervision with a learnable margin to shape embeddings.
The combined objective removes manual tuning used in focal loss and fixed-margin triplet setups.
evidence_signal: On the large-scale VinDR-Mammo dataset, DITL achieved state-of-the-art whole-image breast density classification with significant gains in accuracy, F1-score, and AUC (p < 0.0001), and it also improved performance on small ROI datasets with the same significance.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the self-supervised feature space and kNN neighborhood purity, so degraded embeddings or dataset shift could weaken the adaptive weighting.
paper_title: Re-thinking Mammography Transfer Learning: The Dataset-Informed Transfer Learning (DITL) Framework for Breast Cancer Screening and Lesion Diagnosis
